newsitem.title: USA: Incstar to be bought by American Standard.
newsitem.headline: Incstar to be bought by American Standard.

text.p: Incstar Corp said it signed a memorandum of understanding to be acquired by American Standard Inc, a unit of American Standard Cos Inc, for $6.32 per share.
Under the merger proposal, Incstar would become part of a newly formed medical systems group within American Standard.

Incstar said Sorin Biomedica SpA, its majority shareholder, has entered into a memorandum of understanding with American Standard regarding the proposed sale of Sorin's European diagnostics division to American Standard.

"The memorandum of understanding between American Standard and Incstar contemplates that the simultaneous closing of the Sorin sale of its European diagnostics division will be a condition to the proposed merger," Incstar said.

The deal is proposed as a one-step cash merger in which each Incstar common share would be converted into a right to receive $6.32 in cash, and Incstar would become a wholly-owned subsidiary of American Standard, the company said.
The memorandum of understanding has been approved by a special committee of independent Incstar directors and by the boards of directors of Incstar and American Standard, it said.
The proposed merger is subject to negotiation, execution and approval of a definitive agreement, Incstar said.

Incstar makes clinical and medical tests. Its sales in 1995 were $45.7 million, making it a small player in the $6 billion global market for products that test for disease in human blood, urine and other materials.
The market is dominated by giants like Abbott Laboratories Inc, Diagnostics Products Corp, Boehringer Mannheim Corp and Baxter International Inc.

Medical diagnostics began moving toward sophisticated automated systems some years ago, led by the largest manufacturers. Incstar was left behind after its in-house effort to develop an automated system failed in 1994.
A sweeping restructuring followed, elevating John Booth to chief executive officer. He said in mid-1995 that Incstar was seeking strategic solutions for its long-term future.
Incstar said in November that it had received U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval to sell its second generation of tests for rubella, cytomegalovirus and herpes simplex.
Sales in its third-quarter ended September 27 were $10.6 million, down from $11.6 million a year earlier. Net income was $986,000, down from $1.0 million a year before.
The Stillwater, Minn.-based company could not be reached for comment.

Piscataway, N.J.-based American Standard is a diversified maker of air conditioning, plumbing and automotive products. It will pay about $50.5 million for the publicly traded shares of Incstar, which constitutes less than half of Incstar's total shares outstanding. Sorin, an affiliate of Fiat SpA, owns the remainder and has reached a separate agreement with American Standard.
